hints.title: Handling Users Without Requests
hints.text: A user who never requested a confirmation message has a confirmation rate of 0.00. Use a left join starting from Signups.

hints.title: Calculating the Confirmation Ratio
hints.text: The confirmation rate is the number of confirmed requests divided by the total number of confirmation requests.

hints.title: Averaging and Rounding
hints.text: Compute the average of a conditional expression where action = "confirmed" yields 1 and other values yield 0, rounded to 2 decimal places with coalesce fallback to 0.00.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT
    s.user_id,
    ROUND(IFNULL(AVG(c.action = 'confirmed'), 0), 2) AS confirmation_rate
FROM Signups s
LEFT JOIN Confirmations c
    ON s.user_id = c.user_id
GROUP BY s.user_id;
```

complexity.time: O(S + C) where S is signups and C is confirmation requests
complexity.space: O(S) space for grouped confirmation rates
variables: S: number of users in Signups
C: number of events in Confirmations
complexity.notes: Left join from signups with conditional average aggregation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: An inner join drops users who never triggered a confirmation message.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping directly on indexed user_id computes rates in a single aggregation pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should use ROUND with 2 decimals and properly default null averages to 0.

solutions.code:
SELECT
    s.user_id,
    ROUND(COALESCE(AVG(CASE WHEN c.action = 'confirmed' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END), 0.0), 2) AS confirmation_rate
FROM Signups s
LEFT JOIN Confirmations c
    ON s.user_id = c.user_id
GROUP BY s.user_id;

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def confirmation_rate(signups: pd.DataFrame, confirmations: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    m = pd.merge(signups, confirmations, on='user_id', how='left')
    m['is_confirmed'] = (m['action'] == 'confirmed').astype(float)
    res = m.groupby('user_id')['is_confirmed'].mean().round(2).reset_index()
    res.rename(columns={'is_confirmed': 'confirmation_rate'}, inplace=True)
    res['confirmation_rate'] = res['confirmation_rate'].fillna(0.0)
    return res
solutions.approach: Left merge and group mean in pandas
